newsitem.title: USA: State/local gov. groups take aim at yield - burning.
newsitem.headline: State/local gov. groups take aim at yield - burning.

text.p: - A coalition of state and local government groups said Thursday they are taking aim at an Internal Revenue Service revenue procedure on yield burning that could cost governments about $1 billion.
The groups, which met together for the first time in 10 years, listed yield burning as one of the top four federal issues they plan to address.

Mark Schwartz, an Oklahoma City council member who is president of the National League of Cities, said the groups plan to submit unified comments against the procedure by mid-January and shortly afterward meet with Deputy Treasurery Secretary Lawrence Summers to present their concerns.
"The rule is nothing more than unfunded mandates," Schwartz said. "My goal is they back off from the rule."
He added that the IRS has failed to show there has been wide-spread abuse of yield burning.

The IRS stunned the municipal bond market in July by announcing that issuers of advanced refunding bond can enter into "closing agreements" with the IRS to head off having the interest on their bonds declared taxable.
The action stemmed from allegations that underwriters overcharged some issuers for U.S. Treasuries bought in the open makret and used in bond refundings -- a practice dubbed yield burning.

In addition to the National League of Cities, the groups meeting in Chicago Thursday were the National Governors' Association, National Conference of State Legislatures, Council of State Governments, National Association of Counties, U.S. Conference of Mayors and International City/County Management Association.
